AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 19, 2019
REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Margarita L. Rios, Mayor
  Luigi Vernola, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Leonard Shryock, Councilmember
 Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
 the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
 subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
 minutes.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
 certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
 matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
 meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
 devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
 documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
 Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
 that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
 has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
 during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
 telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

ROLL CALL
   Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Rios

INVOCATION
  Pastor Eddie Cuen
  Trinity Lutheran Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Sarah Llamas, 5th grade
  Lakeland Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Don Murray upon his retirement for 29 years of service to the City.

  II.  City Council to proclaim November 30 as Small Business Saturday.

  III.  Public Safety Badge Pinning.

  IV.  City Council to recognize Native American Heritage Month.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  Veterans Day Recap.

  2.  Grocery Outlet Bargain Market Grand Opening Highlight.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  November 2 and 5, 2019. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period October 6, 2019 –
  October 19, 2019, in the total amount of $925,252.83. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 30, 2019 – November 13, 2019, in the total amount of $2,649,862.82. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Ronald Acosta,
  Sally Arambula, Omar Harrison, and Jeanette Luna. 830-01/08/12

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – November 13, 2019 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 19-80 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – HUMAN RESOURCES
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-80, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN
  RECORDS IN THE HUMAN RESOURCES DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  7.  AWARD OF CONTRACT - CITYWIDE PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT PROGRAM UPDATE – Staff
  recommends City Council award a contract to Bucknam Infrastructure Group, Inc. in the amount of
  $59,983 for Professional Engineering Services for the Pavement Management System Update; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding
  in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1045-04

  Report

  8.  AWARD OF CONTRACT - FLOORING AND BLEACHER REPLACEMENTS AT THE NORWALK ARTS
  AND SPORTS COMPLEX (NASC) – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with McWil
  Sports Surfaces, Inc. in the amount of $302,423 for new hardwood flooring and bleacher replacements
  at the Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement
  and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7852/7853

  Report

  9.  AWARD OF CONTRACT - HEATING, VENTILATION, AND AIR CONDITIONING (HVAC)
  REPLACEMENTS FOR TEEN CENTER, AQUATIC PAVILION AND SOCIAL SERVICES CENTER -
  Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Tri-West Mechanical, Inc. in the amount of
  $41,945 for the installation of new heating, ventilation, and air conditioning units at the Teen Center,
  Aquatic Pavilion and Social Services Center; and authorize the City Manager to execute the contract
  and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7796

  Report

  10. AWARD OF CONTRACTS - EMERGENCY STREET LIGHT MAINTENANCE SERVICE PROVIDER
   AND STREET LIGHT POLE REPLACEMENTS – Staff recommends City Council approve agreements
  with Siemens Mobility, Inc. and Computer Service Company to provide emergency street light
  maintenance and street light pole replacements for the term of the effective date of the agreement
  through June 30, 2021; with the option to extend for two (2) additional one (1) year periods; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the contract and any amendments provided there is funding in
  the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1030

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 19-75 - AMENDING THE CITY OF NORWALK POLICY FOR SMALL WIRELESS
  FACILITIES; AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-76 - AMENDING STANDARD POLE LICENSE AGREEMENT
  FORM TO BE UTILIZED FOR THE INSTALLATION OF A NEW SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY ON
  CITY-OWNED INFRASTRUCTURE – THIS ITEM IS BEING CONTINUED TO DECEMBER 3, 2019.

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 19-77 – PETITION FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE
  – 10800 BLOCK OF LEFFINGWELL ROAD (NORTH SIDE), BETWEEN STUDEBAKER ROAD AND
  LEIBACHER AVENUE AND (SOUTH SIDE), BETWEEN 10860 LEFFINGWELL ROAD AND
  LEIBACHER AVENUE – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-77, A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS FINDING OF FACT
  AND APPROVING THE INSTALLATION OF THE PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE FOR THE 10800
  BLOCK OF LEFFINGWELL ROAD (NORTH SIDE), BETWEEN STUDEBAKER ROAD AND
  LEIBACHER AVENUE AND (SOUTH SIDE), BETWEEN 10860 LEFFINGWELL ROAD AND
  LEIBACHER AVENUE. 1050-02-02

  Report

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 19-78 – PETITION FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE
  – 11300 BLOCK OF FERINA STREET, BETWEEN GRIDLEY ROAD AND GRAYSTONE AVENUE -
  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 19-78, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS FINDING OF FACT AND APPROVING THE
  INSTALLATION OF THE PREFERENTIAL PARKING ZONE FOR THE 11300 BLOCK OF FERINA
  STREET, BETWEEN GRIDLEY ROAD AND GRAYSTONE AVENUE. 1050-02-02

  Report

  15. ADOPTION OF A MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION; RESOLUTION NO. 19-79 - ADOPTING
  GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT NO. 178, ORDINANCE NO. 19-1711 - ADOPTING TEXT
  AMENDMENT NO. 319 AMENDING THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH A LIVE
  WORK OVERLAY ZONE AND REGULATIONS FOR THE SAME, AND ORDINANCE NO. 19-1712 -
  ADOPTING ZONE CHANGE NO. 357 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt the Initial Study and Mitigated Negative Declaration with Mitigation Monitoring Program;

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 19-79, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK RECOMMENDING CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT
  NO. 178;

  c.  introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 19-1711, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING TITLE 17 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH LIVE-WORK
  OVERLAY ZONE AND REGULATIONS FOR THE LIVE-WORK OVERLAY ZONE, by title only
  and waive further reading; and

  d.  introduce for first reading Ordinance No. 19-1712, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
   SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION APPROVING ZONE CHANGE NO.
  357, by title only and waive further reading. 320-02-01/05/09

  Report

REPORTS

  16. AWARD OF CONTRACT - WATER SYSTEM VALUATION – Staff recommends City Council award a
  contract to Stetson Engineers Inc. in the amount of $39,000 to perform an Asset Valuation of the
  Artesia Service Area of the Norwalk Municipal Water System; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1070-05

  Report

  17. POLICY DIRECTION FOR THE 2020 CONSOLIDATED PLAN AND FISCAL YEAR 2020/21 ANNUAL
  ACTION PLAN – Staff recommends City Council direct staff to prepare the Consolidated Plan, Analysis
  of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice and Fiscal Year 2020/21 Annual Action Plan for City Council
  adoption as proposed. 315

  Report

  18. SENIOR NUTRITION PROGRAM QUARTERLY REPORT - Receive and file. 425-02-03

  Report

  19. RESOLUTION NO. 19-81 – APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AND THE NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION - GENERAL AND
  HOURLY UNITS FROM JULY 1, 2019 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2021 AND RESOLUTION NO. 19-82
  APPROVING THE SALARY SCHEDULE INCORPORATING ONE PERCENT COST OF LIVING
  ADJUSMENT AND THE CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE INCREASE EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 29,
  2019 – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 19-81, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AND THE NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION - GENERAL AND HOURLY UNITS

  b.  Resolution No. 19-82, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE SALARY SCHEDULE INCORPORATING THE ONE PERCENT COST OF
  LIVING ADJUSMENT AND THE CALIFORNIA MINIMUM WAGE INCREASE EFFECTIVE
  DECEMBER 29, 2019. 135-09

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated November 14, 2019.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
